items.reason: Pinning a tag to a digest means asking GitHub what that tag points at right now and this session has no network; the repository already ships the exact tool for it (`npm run actions:pin`, which resolves every ref AND flips STRICT/RATCHET in the same pass), so the honest remaining work is one networked run, not a code change.

issue-dispatch.yml's `draft` job held `contents: write` and `pull-requests: write` together; it is now `push` (contents: write, no checkout-independent speech) and `open` (pull-requests: write, no checkout at all), handing the branch name/subject/body between them as an artifact, with a unit test that fails any job in any workflow holding both scopes.

The installed prepare-commit-msg hook now writes lane provenance beside the authorship trailer — `Agent-Harness` always (enforced at commit-msg time, `unknown` when nothing identifies itself) plus `Agent-Model`/`Agent-Spec`/`Agent-Session`/`Agent-Lane` when the environment states them and never guessed; `commit:check --range` reports coverage by harness, and issue-dispatch writes its own trailers because it commits where no hook runs.

A performance budget's numbers have to be measured, and this session has no shell to run `next build` or Playwright; inventing thresholds gives either a budget that never fires or a red CI, which is the same error as inventing an action SHA. The measurement is one `npm run build` away and the repo's own docs:staleness ladder (registry shape blocks, count reports until accepted with `--accept --reason`) is the shape it should take.

The review's four surfaces were already fenced and drilled (scripts/injection-drill.mjs, 8 corpus cases, blocking containment + weekly live refusal), but the harness's OTHER model surface was not: issue-dispatch fenced an `issue` surface inline that no corpus case, no containment check and no live drill had ever seen — and its answer becomes files pushed by a job holding `contents: write`. That surface is now built through the shared fencing builder, covered by three hostile fixtures, and rehearsed under its own system prompt.

The seam itself is easy; making it OPERATE is not. A flag registry with no flags is a stub, and every boolean env toggle already in src/ is either permanent integration config or sits in a CODEOWNERS law file (src/lib/plans.ts, src/lib/llm/) that this task did not ask me to touch. Choosing which shipped feature lands dark first — and therefore what the first registry entry gates — is a product call for the operator, not something to infer.

Every fence blocked and none recorded ever blocking anything — the contract ledger's own `$breaches` note says every `breaches` array is empty because filling one needed a manual pass. The gates now append to a rolling trail on the way out (printRemedy for the check:ci chain, per-rule for the ten SAST rules), and `npm run fences` reads it back next to each fence's exception list and the git date that list last moved, published weekly into the review's existing trail issue.

lessons: This repo's gates are heavily interlocked: adding a stage to `check:ci` also requires a gate-remedy CHAIN entry, a constraint-map row, and a gate-timings baseline, or three other gates go red. Enforcing a new invariant through a test-unit file instead is the repo's own lower-coupling precedent (test-unit/docs-staleness.test.mjs, test-unit/constraint-map.test.mjs) and is what an agent without a test runner should reach for.

Before building anything here, grep for the artefact first — the repository very often already has the tool and is missing only the one networked or measured run that would arm it. `scripts/actions-pin.mjs` pins every action AND flips its own STRICT flag in one pass and has simply never been run; `.github/contract-ledger.json` has had an empty `breaches` array per rule since it landed. Both read as absent practices in a scan and are actually unarmed ones.

A registry-shaped fix is only real if it has a first entry. A feature-flag seam, a perf budget or a golden with no measured baseline scores as a practice and operates as a stub — and in this repo the honest ladder for that is ADR-0007: the registry's SHAPE blocks from day one, the count reports until someone accepts a measured baseline with `--accept --reason`.

When splitting a workflow job for least privilege, check whether the narrow half needs a checkout at all. Dropping `actions/checkout` from the `pull-requests: write` job made it structurally unable to see the source tree, which is a stronger guarantee than any permission line — `gh` only needed `GH_REPO`.
